findings.summary: Server OCR transport reuses parser and byte-limit policy but duplicates the OCR asset path builder instead of sharing the established facsimile OCR URL helper.
findings.consequence: Server SSR/API OCR fetches and client-side facsimile OCR fetches can drift if OCR URL encoding or validation changes, leaving one path requesting or allowlisting a different asset than the other.
findings.evidence: The owned import block at lines 3-6 imports only maximumReaderOcrBytes and parseReaderOcrOverlay from shared/utils/reader-ocr. The module body then builds `/txt/${encodeURIComponent(workId)}/ocr_${filename}.html` locally, while app/lib/reader-facsimile-page.ts uses shared/utils/facsimile-source.ts facsimileOcrUrl(workId, pageIndex), which also centralizes page-index validation and RFC3986 segment encoding.
findings.recommendation: Import facsimileOcrUrl from shared/utils/facsimile-source and use it for the server OCR path before prefixing with base, so server and client OCR fetches share one request-builder and allowlist identity.
